implementation.argument_surface: Three arguments, and each is machine-observed rather than guessed. The receiver arrives in ECX (0x00a85071 MOV ESI,ECX) and is the target of the body's only store, at +0x10 (0x00a85087). The first ordinary stack word is the owner: 0x00a85073 reads it with the displacement 0x08 taken against ESP = entry-4 (the prologue's PUSH ESI), so it lands on entry_ESP + 4, and it is the argument the first indirect call receives in ECX unchanged (0x00a8507c) and whose leading word the body dereferences once (0x00a85077). The second ordinary stack word exists only because the terminator is RET 0xc, which consumes the return address plus two words; no instruction in the body names it, so it is declared, left unnamed in the definition, and its type is not claimed. None of the three arguments is pushed by this body, so nothing about an outgoing call is implied.
implementation.return_note: A 4-byte value. 0x00a85087 stores the dword in EAX to the receiver's +0x10 and the epilogue (POP ESI; RET 0xc) leaves EAX alone, so the returned word and the stored word are the same value; the model test asserts that identity in both directions. The abi record classifies the return as unclassified_in_EAX and no record gives it a C++ type, so the raw word is declared and nothing more.
implementation.receiver_model: An opaque 0x6c-byte run with NO named member. This body touches exactly one thing on it: the dword at +0x10, written at 0x00a85087. It reads nothing, and it writes nothing else. The 0x6c size is not this body's evidence -- on its own the body would bound the object at 0x14 -- it is the minimum from the constructor 0x00a853b0, whose last scalar write is MOV dword ptr [ESI + 0x68], 0xffffffff at 0x00a8544d. That second listing is cited as such in the header and in the model, and no other constructor field is turned into a member.
implementation.dispatch_model: Two sites, both shaped MOV reg, [base + displacement] followed by CALL reg, and both with a single register argument in ECX and no stack argument. Site 1 (0x00a85077 / 0x00a85079 / 0x00a8507c): base = *owner, displacement 0x20, receiver = owner. Site 2 (0x00a8507e / 0x00a85082 / 0x00a85085): base = *(*owner), displacement 0x60, receiver = *owner. The two bases are one and the same address reached by two dereferences, so the chase is two levels deep from the owner and not two independent objects. The model names the fetch helper load_slot and does not claim that both displacements are vtable slots: 0x60 is certainly a slot of a dispatch table, while 0x20 is either the owner's vtable slot 8 (making site 1 an ordinary virtual call) or a callback word inside a callback holder, and the three instructions are identical under both readings.
implementation.dependency_note: No direct callee exists, so the header declares no extern callee. What it does declare is IndirectCall, the shape of an indirect call, which the listing fixes: a 4-byte target read out of memory, one register argument, and a 4-byte EAX result. The model threads ONE explicit EAX word through the body (exposed as eax_register()) because 0x00a8507e re-reads through the post-call EAX instead of reloading [ECX] -- see mechanics.post_call_eax_dependence. That word is model instrumentation, not a machine global.

mechanics.body_shape: Straight-line, 13 instructions, zero conditional branches, zero unconditional branches, zero loops, no exception frame, no stack argument of its own. There is no arm, no guard and no early exit, so the observable behaviour is identical on every call: dereference the owner once, call through the word at +0x20 of what it points at with the owner as the argument, dereference the post-call EAX once, call through the word at +0x60 of that with the post-call EAX as the argument, store the result at the receiver's +0x10, and return it.
mechanics.owner_read: 0x00a85077 MOV EAX,dword ptr [ECX] with ECX = the first stack argument. One dword read at displacement 0. The value is then used as an ADDRESS in two roles: as a table base at +0x20 (0x00a85079) and as a receiver (0x00a85080). A reconstruction that read a member of the owner here, or that treated the owner itself as the table, would be dereferencing a different object; the model test plants a live decoy table at the owner's +0x04 and +0x08 for that.

mechanics.post_call_eax_dependence: The single most important fact about this body, and the reason the model keeps an explicit EAX word instead of writing the natural C++. 0x00a8507e is MOV EDX,dword ptr [EAX] and 0x00a85080 is MOV ECX,EAX: the body does NOT reload [ECX] after the first indirect call. Site 2's receiver AND its table base are therefore whatever site 1's callee left in EAX. Under __thiscall EAX is caller-saved, so a callee is free to have written it, and a source-level reconstruction that re-read arg1->field_00 there is a DIFFERENT function in that case. The model therefore threads one explicit word (exposed as eax_register()) and the model test drives the first observer both ways: preserving EAX keeps the nominal path, and clobbering EAX must move the second dispatch onto a decoy object and a decoy table. Whether the REAL callee at +0x20 preserves EAX is not determinable from this body; it is the first unresolved question.
mechanics.slot_index_arithmetic: 0x20 / 4 == 8 and 0x60 / 4 == 0x18. Recorded as arithmetic identities, not as second evidence, and asserted by nothing in the model.
mechanics.store: 0x00a85087 89 46 10 -- a 3-byte dword store, MOV dword ptr [ESI + 0x10], EAX. It is the body's only memory write. It is not a byte or halfword store, not a store through a pointer the calls returned, and not an increment or an exchange: the EAX value replaces the old word. It happens after both calls return, which the model test measures by having each observer read the receiver's +0x10 as it is entered.
mechanics.return_semantics_machine: EAX at 0x00a85087 is site 2's return value, the same word that is stored. 0x00a8508a POP ESI and 0x00a8508b RET 0xc touch no general-purpose register that carries a result, so the caller receives exactly the word that was stored. The identity returned == stored is asserted by the model test.
mechanics.receiver_writes: One dword at the receiver's +0x10 and nothing else. The model test compares the receiver's whole 0x6c bytes before and after the call and requires that only bytes 0x10..0x13 changed, so 'no other byte changed' is asserted rather than assumed.
mechanics.not_modelled: The PUSH ESI / POP ESI pair (a frame fact with no observable in C++), the callee-owned argument pop, and the register names themselves, which the model reproduces through its single EAX word rather than through a register abstraction.
mechanics.globals: None. No instruction in the 13 names a data-segment address. The constructor 0x00a853b0 does read five constants (0x01677d7c, 0x01677d80, 0x01677d84, 0x01485720, 0x1677e28) but those are the constructor's evidence and none of them appears in this body.
mechanics.vtable_membership: This body is itself an entry of vtable 0x01458024, at byte offset +0 (slot 0), and that is checked here three ways rather than taken from the association: (a) the dword at 0x01458024 read out of the image is 0x00a85070; (b) the ONLY reference to 0x01458024 in the whole program is the DATA xref from 0x00a853d8, inside the constructor 0x00a853b0, whose instruction is MOV dword ptr [ESI], 0x1458024 -- i.e. the class installs this table on its own receiver at +0x00; (c) the 15 entries read from 0x01458024 to 0x0145805c are 0x00a85070, 0x004ae250, 0x00a850d0, 0x00a85790, 0x007edc60, 0x00a858c0, 0x00a85840, 0x00951230, 0x0082e640, 0x00950ea0, 0x0082e650, 0x0082e650, 0x0082e650, 0x0082e650, 0x0051e340, 0x0051e380, followed by the strings 'user8', 'user7', 'user6', 'user5'. Nothing before 0x01458024 is a code pointer (0x0145801c is 0x00000034 and 0x01458020 is 0x4b400000, a float), so the table starts where the record says it does. The body itself never reads a dispatch word on ITS OWN receiver, so nothing at receiver+0x00 is named in the model.
mechanics.receiver_context_from_other_bodies: Context only, and deliberately NOT turned into members. The same constructor 0x00a853b0 also installs a second vtable at the receiver's +0x04 (MOV dword ptr [ESI + 0x4], 0x14599e8 at 0x00a853de), which is the multiple-inheritance base of the class, and it zeroes +0x10 (MOV dword ptr [ESI + 0x10], EAX with EAX = 0 at 0x00a853e5). Two of the sibling entries of the same vtable then read that word as a pointer to a polymorphic object and dispatch on it: 0x00a850d0 does MOV ECX,[ESI+0x10] (0x00a850dd), TEST ECX,ECX / JZ (0x00a850e5..e7) and then MOV EAX,[ECX] / MOV EDX,[EAX + 0x18] / CALL EDX (0x00a850f7..fc); 0x00a85790 does CMP dword ptr [ESI + 0x10],0 (0x00a8579d) and the same +0x18 dispatch (0x00a857de..e6), and further dispatches through +0x1c, +0x14, +0x10 and +0x0c of the same object. mechanics.class_identity: Not established, and deliberately not guessed. The vtable's 15 entries plus the constructor's own member set (two vtables, a pointer at +0x0c taken from the constructor's argument, a zeroed +0x10, a flag byte at +0x14, floats at +0x18/+0x1c/+0x20, zeroed halfwords at +0x24/+0x26, floats at +0x28..+0x34, an initialised member at +0x38, floats at +0x5c/+0x60/+0x64 and -1 at +0x68) are enough to recognise the SHAPE and not the NAME. return_semantics.value: The value site 2's callee leaves in EAX, which 0x00a85087 stores at the receiver's +0x10 and which the epilogue returns unchanged. The model declares the raw Word and does not claim whether it is a pointer, a count, a handle or an id.
return_semantics.ownership: Not applicable: the body allocates nothing and returns no address of its own. The returned word is whatever the callee produced.
return_semantics.lifetime: The value is produced by a callee this body does not own and stores it into a field of a receiver it does not own, so its lifetime is the callee's and the field's, not this body's. The two sibling bodies of the same vtable go on to dispatch through the stored word, which is the only hint about its meaning.

unresolved_questions: Does the real callee at the +0x20 fetch preserve EAX? The body depends on it -- 0x00a8507e and 0x00a85080 both read the post-call EAX rather than reloading [ECX] -- and nothing in this body can show it. The model reproduces the machine either way and the model test drives both behaviours; what is missing is evidence about the actual callee, which lives outside this body.

Is the word at the dispatch object's +0x20 a vtable slot of the owner (making site 1 an ordinary virtual call on the owner) or a callback word stored in a callback-holder object and invoked with the owner as its single argument? Both readings execute the identical three instructions at 0x00a85079, 0x00a8507c and the surrounding frame, so the listing cannot separate them and the model asserts neither.

What is the second stack word? It exists only because the terminator is RET 0xc. No instruction reads entry_ESP + 0x8, there is no call site to inspect (the body has no direct callers), and no record constrains it, so its type and its value are unconstrained here.

What are the C++ types, and what is the class? The vtable 0x01458024, its 15 entries and the constructor's member set fix the receiver's SHAPE but not its name, and no SDK association was corroborated for this VA. In particular 0x004ae250, which shares the table, is a 7-instruction no-op, so the name another package attached to it is not supported by its bytes.

Is the returned/stored word a pointer? Two sibling entries of the same vtable treat the receiver's +0x10 as a pointer to a polymorphic object, which makes it very likely -- but this body never reads that word, so its type is not fixed by this listing and the model leaves the slot opaque.

The receiver's layout above the single +0x10 store is taken from the constructor 0x00a853b0, not from this body. On its own this body bounds the object at 0x14 only. Any claim about a member beyond +0x10 rests on that second listing.
No decompilation exists for this VA in this session (three decompiler calls all failed), so no decompiler disagreement could be recorded and no decompiler observation backs the reconstruction.

Two of the vtable's later entries (0x0082e650, x4, and 0x0051e340 / 0x0051e380) were not disassembled, so whether the table is one homogeneous interface list or a mix of the class's own and inherited methods is not established. It does not affect this body, which is slot 0.

conditions: The original process is driven far enough to call this body through vtable 0x01458024 slot 0 with a live owner object.

A trace records the word at owner+0x00, the target fetched at 0x00a85079, the value in EAX immediately after 0x00a8507c returns, the word that 0x00a8507e then reads, the target fetched at 0x00a85082, and the dword written at 0x00a85087.

The decisive measurement is that EAX value: if it still equals owner+0x00, the body is insensitive to the first callee's EAX and the natural source-level re-read would have been equivalent; if it does not, the first unresolved question is answered and the re-read reconstruction is refuted.

The trace must also show whether the second callee is a virtual call on the object at *owner (whose +0x00 is the base) or a call through a field, which is what would settle the second unresolved question from the callee side.
Until a trace exists, RUNTIME stays GATED at 0 and nothing in this package may be promoted on the strength of a static pass alone.

mutation_checking.survivors: 0 of 30. Nothing in this body's model is left unconstrained by the test.
mutation_checking.known_limits: Five of the thirty die on a SIGSEGV rather than on an assertion, and the reason is a property of the fixture, not a hole in the test: a decoy word that is a TABLE pointer, used where the model expects a CALL TARGET, makes the machine execute the fixture as code, and no C++ object can be both a valid function entry and a table with a live slot at +0x60. The test therefore plants decoys chosen for the role a wrong displacement would put them in -- table pointers at the words a wrong second-base read would pick up, function pointers at the words a wrong first-target fetch would pick up -- so each wrong word is caught by a named assertion in the role it can actually reach, and the remaining cross-role shape (M20) is killed by a fault. Four of the five print 14 assertion failures before faulting. Second limit: the sinks make a wrong path keep dereferencing valid memory, so a mutation that walks the whole chain wrongly can reach a live observer and be reported by name; that is stronger than a fault but it is still an assertion about the test's own observers, not about the original process.
